creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The broad matrix of common keys (Tests/MusterVTTests/KeyEncoderTests.swift) is a rendered snapshot rather than conformance cases, deliberately: it is one matrix with one reason rather than nineteen behaviors, and its oracle is libghostty upstream, so nineteen per-case 'why' fields would be manufactured rationale.

But the keystroke *list* still lives in Swift, which means a Rust port hand-copies nineteen entries - exactly the drift the corpus exists to prevent. Low risk, because the snapshot cross-checks it: if Rust renders the same file, the list matched. Worth closing anyway.

Shape: a 'survey' section in corpus/conformance/key-encoder.json carrying the profiles and the keystroke list, with each language's driver rendering it to the same snapshot. Needs corpus-lint to know that section is legitimate and still enforce the why rule on 'cases'.
title: Move the key-encoder survey's keystroke list into data
